---
title: "Zero-passing-stall accession analysis"
subtitle: "260807 75x75 run — trueRef, G6-dedup, calibrated NB null, SF>=0.3"
output: html_document
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
```

## Load data

```{r load}
df <- read_csv("zero_pass_accessions_summary.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    depth_tier = factor(
      depth_tier,
      levels = c("Underpowered (<100)", "Ambiguous (100-1000)", "Well-powered, negative (>=1000)")
    ),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("10mM", "01mM"))
  )

glimpse(df)
```

## Summary counts

```{r summary-counts}
df %>%
  count(condition, depth_tier, name = "n_accessions") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = depth_tier, values_from = n_accessions, values_fill = 0)
```

## Stacked bar: depth tier x primary fail reason

```{r stacked-bar, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
ggplot(df, aes(x = depth_tier, fill = primary_fail_reason)) +
  geom_bar(color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~condition) +
  labs(
    title = "Reasons for zero passing stalls, by coverage tier",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of accessions",
    fill = "Primary fail reason"
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## Read-depth distribution (continuous, log scale)

A complementary view to the fixed tiers above — shows the actual continuum
rather than three hard-cutoff buckets, in case the tier boundaries (100 /
1000 reads) feel arbitrary relative to the real distribution shape.

```{r depth-continuous, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
ggplot(df, aes(x = max_depth_reads, fill = primary_fail_reason)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) +
  facet_wrap(~condition, ncol = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(100, 1000), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  labs(
    title = "Best-replicate read depth for zero-pass accessions",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines mark the 100 / 1000-read tier boundaries",
    x = "Max reads across replicates (log scale)",
    y = "Number of accessions",
    fill = "Primary fail reason"
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

## The requested list: well-powered, high depth, but negative

Accessions with >=1000 reads in their best replicate that still failed
purely on `low_stall_reads` (G1) or `low_treated_sf` (G2) -- i.e. genuinely
well-sequenced accessions with no detectable Xrn1 stall signal above
threshold. These are the most defensible candidate biological negatives
in the dataset (as opposed to accessions that simply lacked coverage).

```{r well-powered-table}
well_powered <- df %>%
  filter(depth_tier == "Well-powered, negative (>=1000)") %>%
  arrange(condition, desc(max_depth_reads))

well_powered %>%
  select(condition, accession, max_depth_reads, primary_fail_reason,
         family, genus, species)
```

```{r well-powered-export}
write_csv(well_powered, "well_powered_negative_accessions.csv")
```

### By family

Worth checking whether these negatives cluster within particular viral
families/genera -- a real taxonomic pattern (e.g. "no resistance detected
in any well-covered member of genus X") is a more interesting and
reportable result than an unstructured accession list.

```{r by-family, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
well_powered %>%
  filter(!is.na(family), family != "", family != "Unannotated") %>%
  count(condition, family, sort = TRUE) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(family, n), y = n, fill = condition)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Well-powered, negative accessions by viral family",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of accessions",
    fill = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

## Notes / caveats

- Depth tiers use each accession's **best** (highest read-count) replicate,
  not an average -- an accession only needs to be well-powered in *one*
  replicate to be considered "well-powered, negative" here, which is the
  most charitable reading of the data before calling something a real
  negative.
- `primary_fail_reason` is the first-listed failure reason from that best
  replicate's `fail_reason` string (numeric thresholds stripped for
  grouping); an accession may have failed multiple gates simultaneously,
  but only the first is shown here.
- This tier scheme (`<100` / `100-1000` / `>=1000` reads) is a starting
  heuristic, not a statistically derived cutoff -- reconsider these
  boundaries if the continuous histogram above suggests a different
  natural break.
